units.function: open on a shared belief, then state the quantitative goal against it

original_instantiations: From the trained critics to the loudest fans, everyone is sure they can name the best work and the best years. We set out to use the records of who shaped whom, and of what the work actually sounds like, to read the last century of the field in numbers.

Experts and amateurs alike think they already know which names and which decades matter most. Our aim was to put the record of influence and the record of sound to work and measure the history instead of arguing it.

units.source_excerpt: From trained musicologists to outspoken hipsters, everyone believes they know the greatest musicians and greatest periods of music. Our goal was to use data describing artist influence and sound content in order to perform a quantitative analysis of the last 90 years of musical history.
units.reusable_pattern: From [expert] to [amateur], everyone believes they know [the thing]. Our goal was to use data describing [two sources] in order to perform a quantitative analysis of [the span].
reusable_elements: occurrences: summary, first paragraph.
stable function: set a confident consensus against a measured answer.
pattern: everyone believes they know / Our goal was to.
boundary: the consensus must be one the data can actually test.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the field or the span.
Do not mock the consensus; the sentence only sets it up.

units.function: open the method with the first thing sought and the count of kinds

features.clause_structure: one sentence with a colon list
original_instantiations: First, we set out to name the most influential names by keeping four separate kinds of influence apart: the direct kind, the indirect kind, the kind inside a group, and the kind that crosses groups.
To begin, we tried to rank the biggest names while holding four sorts of influence distinct, from the close and direct to the broad and cross-cutting.

units.source_excerpt: First, we sought to identify the most influential artists by considering four distinct types of influence: direct, indirect, within genre, and across genre.
units.reusable_pattern: First, we sought to identify [the target] by considering [a count] distinct types of [the thing]: [list].
reusable_elements: occurrences: summary, second paragraph.
stable function: announce the first sub-goal with an enumerated split.
pattern: First, we sought to / by considering N distinct types.
boundary: the types must stay distinct later, not collapse.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not copy the four type names.

units.function: turn a failed test into the motive for the next method

original_instantiations: The classifier only worked once we cut the labels down to the four biggest groups. That miss pushed us to cluster the sound space itself and build our own groupings, a view of the field that ignores the usual labels.

It sorted the records correctly only after we kept just the largest categories. The failure is what led us to group the sound data directly and name fresh categories that owe nothing to the familiar ones.

units.source_excerpt: It did not accurately predict established genres unless we limited the number of genres to the four largest. This failure inspired us to use k-means clustering on the sonic variable space to create original sonic genres, offering a perspective on music which is agnostic of familiar labels.
units.reusable_pattern: It did not accurately predict [the target] unless we limited [the scope]. This failure inspired us to [the next method], offering a perspective which is agnostic of [the usual labels].
reusable_elements: occurrences: summary, third paragraph.
stable function: make a negative result the reason for the next model.
pattern: unless we limited / This failure inspired us to / agnostic of.
boundary: the failure must be reported before it is used as motive.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not name the algorithm or the label set.

units.function: close by reading the unmatched cases as a finding, not a miss

original_instantiations: We also guessed that the shifts which did not line up with the written history are the quieter changes our measure caught and the usual histories missed.
The breaks that matched no known event, we suggest, are the subtle ones, visible only because we did not rely on the standard categories.

units.source_excerpt: We also speculated that the revolutions which did not clearly align with known history represent more subtle developments in music captured by our model.
units.reusable_pattern: We also speculated that the [cases] which did not clearly align with [the record] represent more subtle [developments] captured by our model.
reusable_elements: occurrences: summary, last paragraph.
stable function: convert a non-match into a claim about subtlety.
pattern: We also speculated that / did not clearly align / captured by our model.
boundary: mark it as speculation, never as a confirmed result.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not treat the unmatched cases as proof.

units.function: open the problem as a question of scale

original_instantiations: Where do you start when the task is to see how thousands of people shaped one another across the better part of a century?

units.source_excerpt: How does one begin to understand the way in which 5854 artists influenced each other over the span of 90 years?

pattern: How does one begin to understand the way in which.

prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the count or the field.

units.function: answer the opening question with the first concrete step

units.function: report the first structural facts before any model

units.function: state one assumption and give its reason in the same breath

original_instantiations: We take an actor's first decade as their most influential point, because the people who start a shift tend to do it early in their career.
We treat the opening decade as the peak of influence, on the grounds that those who drive a change usually do so at the start.

units.function: concede that a choice is arbitrary before defending the one made

original_instantiations: Any choice here is a judgement call. We keep every factor equal so that no one factor is favoured by fiat.

units.function: wish for a validation the nature of the inquiry blocks

units.function: generalize from one gap to the character of the whole inquiry
